subject: Hybrid billing proposal for PulseHealth VPC pilot
messages:
From: Asha Menon <asha.menon@pulsehealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@pulsehealth.com
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2024 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment pilot — pricing questions and packaging

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the demo this week. Procurement and engineering are aligned on a small VPC/on-prem pilot (3 months) to validate latency and regional orchestration. A few questions from our side to help the internal buy:

- Can you lay out two commercial options we can present to finance: (A) node-anchored credits (prepaid node credits + lower platform fee) vs (B) consumption-first (metered tokens with a higher platform fee amortized over the pilot)?
- How do support tiers map to response SLOs for on-prem? We need an on-call escalation path for P1 incidents during pilot hours (M-F 6am–8pm PT).
- Any discounts available for a three-site pilot (US-east, US-west, EU) with a 6-month conversion commitment?

Attached is our short RFP and a procurement template. If you could send a short comparison deck and a ballpark, that would be great — procurement hopes to review next week.

Thanks,
Asha

Attachments: PulseHealth_RFP_Q4.pdf (11 pages)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Asha Menon <asha.menon@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 19 Apr 2024 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment pilot — pricing questions and packaging

Hi Asha — great to hear procurement is moving this along. Below is a concise comparison we can present to finance; I attached an XLS with line-item math (RH_Pulsehealth_pricing_scenarios.xlsx).

Summary (pilot: 3 months, 3 sites):

Option A — Node-anchored credits
- Purchase node credits for each site (prepaid for pilot).
- Platform fee: lower (35% of standard platform fee, amortized monthly for pilot).
- Pros: predictable spend, easier capacity planning, simpler offline/on-prem operator licensing.
- Cons: higher upfront OPEX/CapEx during pilot; less ideal if utilization is low.
- Ballpark: 6 node-credits/site for pilot month 1, 3 node-credits/month thereafter; estimated $75k total pilot cost before discounts.

Option B — Consumption-first (metered)
- Monthly metered usage (tokens + embeddings) billed against a platform fee that is higher (full platform fee) but credits applied monthly to smooth start-up.
- Pros: lower upfront, better if usage is spiky; easier to align with pay-as-you-go workloads.
- Cons: forecasting variance; unit price slightly higher.
- Ballpark: estimated $55k total pilot cost (assuming 20M tokens/month aggregate) before discounts.

Support mapping (pilot):
- Standard Pilot Support (included): M-F 6am–6pm PT monitoring and case triage, 24-hour P1 response from engineering on business-day.
- Premium Pilot On-call (add-on): M-F 6am–8pm PT guaranteed 2-hour initial response, direct SRE escalation + weekly alignment call — additional $8k/month.

Discounts and conversion credits:
- Three-site pilot: we can extend a 12% pilot bundle discount to either option A or B.
- If PulseHealth converts to an annual committed plan within 6 months after pilot, we can apply a conversion credit equal to 20% of pilot invoice toward the first quarterly invoice.

Next steps:
1) I’ll loop in Marissa for exact list pricing and to lock a DocuSign SOW.
2) We can run a short SLA addendum for the pilot window (Irene will scope observability & incident playbooks).

If you want a single-page comparison slide, I can send that to procurement by end of day.

Thanks — Diego

- Option B (Consumption-first): $48,400 total for 3 months (assumes 20M tokens/month). Includes metered pricing + platform fee, with monthly invoicing.

Thanks team — a couple of compliance and SOW notes for procurement review:

- SLA addendum: include P1 response and target MTTR expectations for pilot window; define on-call escalation matrix and who owns runbook updates.
- Observability add-on: include a 30-day trial for the Redwood Console retention (14 days by default, extended to 30 for pilot) so PulseHealth can validate tracing and token-level cost telemetry.
- Legal: recommend a pilot-specific liability cap (equal to pilot fees) and a 30-day opt-out after pilot start if major issues arise (this is a standard protection for both parties).
- Commercial tweak: we can increase the conversion credit to 25% of pilot invoice if PulseHealth commits to a 12-month minimum within 60 days of pilot end.

I’ll draft the SOW language and SLA addendum; Diego/Marissa, if these commercial tweaks are acceptable, I’ll include them in the SOW and mark the DocuSign tag for signature.

—Irene
